pr_body:
Take a slightly hackier but more reliable method of setting up `$HOMEBREW_PREFIX`, `$HOME` and `--appdir`.

- Use constants for placeholders
- Monkeypatch to set `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` consistently to placeholder
- Use environment variable to set `Dir.home` consistently to placeholder
- Use `appdir` short-circuit to set `Cask#appdir` consistently to placeholder
- Use `Cask.generating_hash!` to enable "generating mode" with these patches
- Fix `Formula#caveats` from JSON

See https://github.com/Homebrew/formulae.brew.sh/pull/744 for the formulae.brew.sh side.

Fixes #14505
Fixes #14595

comments: Not sure if relevant: I `bisect`'ed around and got 2a5d41d41be3 as the first bad commit.

Okay, looking a bit further, [there is an issue](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/issues/140870) already filled about it. Try running `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 brew install --cask android-platform-tools`.

> Okay, looking a bit further, [there is an issue](https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/issues/140870) already filled about it. Try running `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 brew install --cask android-platform tools`.

Yes, it works!

Moreover, `HOMEBREW_NO_INSTALL_FROM_API=1 brew info --cask android-platform-tools` also works well.

```

==> Analytics
install: 14,802 (30 days), 43,076 (90 days), 186,551 (365 days)

```

Looks like the JSON doesn't use placeholder for `Artifact::Relocated`, which includes `Artifact::Binary` (`binary` stanza):
https://github.com/Homebrew/brew/blob/1cf53b4281e7bc22a8d7fc915fc6ba4576f8ef88/Library/Homebrew/cask/cask.rb#L301-L304

A couple Casks do have hardcoded paths to `/usr/local` like `dotnet`:
```rb
  binary "/usr/local/share/dotnet/dotnet"
```

There may need to be a way to differentiate these two scenarios. By the time above code is hit, the `#{staged_path}` is already resolved to local system path.

> By the time above code is hit, the `#{staged_path}` is already resolved to local system path.

It doesn't work. After `brew update` twice, I tried `brew reinstall android-platform-tools` and `brew info --cask android-platform-tools`. Both use `/usr/local/` still.
The issue isn't fixed. I only pointed out where it is happening.

For example, existing code will generate JSON with hardcoded paths:
```console
❯ brew info --json=v2 --cask android-platform-tools | jq '.casks[0].artifacts[0]'
{
  "binary": [
    "/opt/homebrew/Caskroom/android-platform-tools/34.0.0/platform-tools/mke2fs"
  ]
}
```

If you locally modify `replace_prefix` option then it can generate portable:
```console
❯ brew info --json=v2 --cask android-platform-tools | jq '.casks[0].artifacts[0]'
{
  "binary": [
    "$(brew --prefix)/Caskroom/android-platform-tools/34.0.0/platform-tools/mke2fs"
  ]
}
```

But this will break other casks so it is not the right way to handle issue.

---

EDIT: Also, any changes will need to be uploaded to API server. You can see copy that is used at https://formulae.brew.sh/api/cask/android-platform-tools.json

So, even after a fix is added, it will need to go live to be available via API.

> There may need to be a way to differentiate these two scenarios. By the time above code is hit, the `#{staged_path}` is already resolved to local system path.

Replacing `/usr/local/Caskroom` sounds like it would be reasonable solution.
Related, but slightly different issue regarding `caskroom_path`: https://github.com/Homebrew/homebrew-cask/issues/140852

> Replacing `/usr/local/Caskroom` sounds like it would be reasonable solution.

That should work for the `staged_path` and `caskroom_path` issue, which covers a lot of Casks.

It won't work for `HOMEBREW_PREFIX` usage like in `android-commandlinetools`:
```rb
  android_sdk_root = "#{HOMEBREW_PREFIX}/share/android-commandlinetools"
  android_clt_dir = "#{android_sdk_root}/cmdline-tools/latest"

  binary "#{android_clt_dir}/bin/apkanalyzer"
```

There is also the separate `appdir` issue, but that is tracked by #14505 and probably less common.
I've implemented a fix that covers most cases. It doesn't cover `android-commandlinetools`, but that's the only one I'm aware of that isn't covered.
